text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000101 bills 99215 far above expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, but the small documented sample supports the billed levels and also shows signs of cloned or inflated notes.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is what upcoding looks like. The elevated 99215 share holds in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one condition, and most 99215s fall there (e.g., C0048984, C0049045, C0049104 coded only Z09). Against that, the records review found documented 99215s supported at a rate well below the comparison providers, which would normally point to a legitimately complex panel. But the panel does not look complex, and some 'supported' notes document high MDM on patients with no chronic conditions and follow-up or abdominal pain codes (C0049321, C0049434). The returned notes also show a high duplicate rate, repeated times and the data-reviewed mismatch code already flagged, all weak signs the notes may be templated to match the billed level rather than the visit. Documentation covers under a tenth of claims and no audit trail was received, so a reviewer should first request audit trails and compare the full text of the supported low-complexity 99215 notes (starting with C0049321 and C0049434) for cloning, then pull a larger records sample weighted toward 0–1 condition 99215 claims."}
